mainTopic: Damaging what is already damaged (חמץ, castration, adding a מום), and liability for leavening that finishes by itself
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא about a sick בכור. One opinion allows letting its blood, and רבי יהודה forbids it even if the animal will die. רבי יוחנן explains where that argument applies. Everyone agrees that leavening an already-leavened מנחה is punishable, and so is castrating an animal that was already castrated. The only argument is about adding a מום to an animal that already has one. רבי מאיר forbids it, based on 'כל מום לא יהיה בו'. The רבנן allow it, based on 'תמים יהיה לרצון'. The גמרא then shows how each side uses the other side's words: רבי מאיר uses 'תמים' for redeemed פסולי המוקדשין, and the רבנן use 'כל מום' to forbid causing a מום indirectly. Finally, רבי אמי rules that someone who puts שאור on a מנחה dough that then rises by itself is חייב, like on שבת. The גמרא begins to challenge this from רבה בר בר חנה, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Letting blood of a sick firstborn: the end of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes: one opinion says the בכור may even be slaughtered because of the wound made by bloodletting. רבי יהודה says you may not let its blood at all, even if it will die.
steps.simpleTranslation: The animal may even be slaughtered because of that blemish. רבי יהודה says: even if it will die, we do not let its blood.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a ברייתא about a בכור that is sick from too much blood. Two opinions are given about whether we may cut it to let out blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Letting blood makes a cut, and a cut can count as a מום (blemish) on the animal. The first opinion says the cut is allowed, and that this מום even lets the animal be slaughtered as a blemished בכור. רבי יהודה says making the cut is never allowed, even if the animal will die without it.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male animal, which is holy and must be given to a כהן
A blemish that makes an animal unfit to be a קרבן
Letting blood: cutting the animal to release extra blood

steps.confusionAlert: This is the end of a quote that started earlier on the דף. The case is a בכור that is sick from too much blood, not a קרבן already on the מזבח.

phrases.english: It may even be slaughtered on account of that blemish.
phrases.notes: 'That blemish' is the cut made when the blood was let.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says:
Even if it would die,
we do not let its blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא that was quoted earlier on the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One opinion allows letting the blood of a sick בכור, and it may then be slaughtered because of that מום. רבי יהודה forbids letting its blood even if it will die.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: leavening an already-leavened מנחה is punishable
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says everyone agrees that someone who leavens a מנחה after someone else already leavened it is חייב. This is because the תורה forbids חמץ in a מנחה twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: everyone agrees that one who leavens after another leavened is liable. It says 'it shall not be made חמץ' and 'it shall not be baked חמץ'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן starts to define the edges of the argument in the ברייתא. He first gives a case where everyone agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dough is already חמץ, so you might think a second person adds nothing new. But the תורה forbids חמץ in a מנחה in two separate פסוקים. This shows that every act of leavening is a new עבירה, even on dough that is already leavened.

keyTerms.meaning: Leavening after someone else already leavened
Leavened dough, forbidden in most מנחות

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the main idea of this section: sometimes you are punished for damaging something that is already damaged.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
All agree about one who leavens after one who leavened,
phrases.notes: 'All' means the חכמים who argue in the ברייתא about the sick בכור.

phrases.english: that he is liable,
as it is written: 'It shall not be made leavened'
and 'It shall not be baked leavened.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts marking out where the argument in the ברייתא does and does not apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leavening a מנחה that is already חמץ is punishable, according to everyone.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: castrating an already-castrated animal is punishable
steps.stepSummary: Everyone also agrees that one who castrates an animal after someone else castrated it is חייב. The source is the פסוק that lists four kinds of castration.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, one who castrates after another castrated is liable, as it is written: 'bruised, crushed, detached, or cut.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second case where everyone agrees. He brings a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works like the חמץ case: doing damage again to an animal already damaged in the same way is still an עבירה. The next step will show exactly how this פסוק teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: One who castrates (destroys an animal's ability to reproduce)

phrases.english: And about one who castrates after one who castrated,
that he is liable,
as it is written: 'Bruised or crushed'
'or detached or cut.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case of agreement, parallel to the חמץ case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Castrating an animal that is already castrated is punishable, according to everyone.

steps.title: How the פסוק teaches castration after castration
steps.stepSummary: If you are חייב for 'cut', you would surely be חייב for 'detached', which is worse. So the word 'detached' must be teaching something new: detaching after someone already cut is also punishable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one is liable for cutting, is he not all the more so liable for detaching? Rather, it comes to include one who detaches after one who cut, that he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the פסוק proves the point from the step before. It uses a קל וחומר to show that one of the words would be extra unless it teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Detaching is a worse injury than cutting, so the תורה did not need to tell us that detaching is forbidden. Since the תורה wrote it anyway, it must be talking about a new case. That case is detaching an animal that was already made sterile by cutting, and the person is still חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not all the more so? (a קל וחומר argument)

steps.whatToRemember: According to everyone, damaging something already damaged can still be punished. This is true for חמץ in a מנחה and for castrating an animal.
steps.confusionAlert: The question 'is he not all the more so liable?' is not an attack on the פסוק. It shows a word that seems extra, so the גמרא can find what that word teaches.

phrases.english: If he is liable for cutting,
for detaching, is it not all the more so?
Rather, it comes to include one who detaches after one who cut,
that he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם עַל כּוֹרֵת הוּא חַיָּיב, עַל נוֹתֵק לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק in the step before proves the rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'נתוק' in ויקרא 22:24 would not be needed because of a קל וחומר, so it must include detaching after cutting.

steps.title: The real argument: adding a מום to an animal that already has one
steps.stepSummary: The only argument is about making a מום on an animal that already has a מום. רבי מאיר forbids it, based on 'כל מום לא יהיה בו'. The רבנן allow it, because 'תמים יהיה לרצון' speaks only about an animal that is still perfect.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue only about one who puts a blemish on a blemished animal. רבי מאיר holds: 'any blemish shall not be in it.' The רבנן hold: 'it shall be perfect to be accepted.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes by pinning down the one case that is argued about. He shows which part of the same פסוק each side relies on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides read ויקרא 22:21. רבי מאיר stresses 'any blemish', so even a second מום on an animal that already has one is forbidden. The רבנן stress 'perfect to be accepted', so the איסור only covers an animal that is still תמים and fit for the מזבח. An animal that already has a מום is not covered.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes (puts) a blemish on an animal
An animal that already has a blemish
'It shall be perfect to be accepted', meaning still fit for a קרבן

steps.whatToRemember: Leavening after leavening and castrating after castrating are punishable according to everyone. The argument is only about adding a מום to a בעל מום: רבי מאיר says forbidden, the רבנן say allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the argument about letting blood from the sick בכור. Once the animal is sick, is it treated like a בעל מום, so that making a cut is allowed?

phrases.english: They argued only
about one who puts a blemish on a blemished animal.
רבי מאיר holds:
'Any blemish shall not be in it.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:21. 'Any' blemish includes even a second one.

phrases.english: And the רבנן hold:
'It shall be perfect to be accepted.'
phrases.notes: The same פסוק. They read it as covering only an animal that is still perfect.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא בְּמֵטִיל מוּם בְּבַעַל מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the cases of agreement, it names the one case that is argued about and gives each side's source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Adding a מום to a בעל מום: רבי מאיר says it is forbidden based on 'כל מום', and the רבנן say it is allowed based on 'תמים יהיה לרצון'.

steps.title: What does רבי מאיר do with the other פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר: the פסוק 'תמים יהיה לרצון' seems to limit the איסור to a perfect animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי מאיר too, isn't it written 'It shall be perfect to be accepted'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks רבי מאיר how he deals with the פסוק that the רבנן used to permit making a מום on a blemished animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן read 'תמים יהיה לרצון' as saying the איסור only applies while the animal is still perfect. If רבי מאיר forbids a מום even on a blemished animal, he must explain what that פסוק is teaching.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Meir as well,
isn't it written: "It shall be perfect to be accepted"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:21. This is the same פסוק the רבנן used in the last step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי מאיר's position from step 5 using the רבנן's פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's view that making a מום on a blemished animal is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'תמים יהיה לרצון' seems to limit the איסור to a perfect animal, so רבי מאיר must account for it.

steps.title: First answer: it excludes an animal born blemished
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that for רבי מאיר, the פסוק excludes an animal that had a מום from the very start.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק comes to exclude an animal that was blemished from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first answer for רבי מאיר: 'תמים' only excludes an animal that was born with a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this answer, an animal born blemished may be given another מום. But an animal that was perfect and later got a מום stays forbidden, which keeps רבי מאיר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that has a blemish
From the start, from the beginning

phrases.english: That verse is to exclude an animal blemished from the start.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the פסוק to a narrower case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'תמים יהיה לרצון' permits a מום on any blemished animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only permits a מום on an animal blemished from birth.

steps.title: An animal born blemished needs no פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first answer: an animal born with a מום is like a palm tree and obviously has no איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal blemished from the start is just like a palm tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the answer of step 7: there is no need for a פסוק to exclude an animal born with a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal born blemished can never become a proper קרבן, so it has no more קדושה of a קרבן than a tree does. Of course you may make a מום on it, so the פסוק cannot be coming to teach that.

phrases.english: An animal blemished from the start —
it is merely a palm tree.
phrases.notes: He means it could never be brought as a קרבן, so it is like any ordinary object.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרָא – דִּיקְלָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer given in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested use of the פסוק for an animal born blemished.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That case is obvious and needs no פסוק, since such an animal never had the קדושה of a קרבן.

steps.title: Final answer: it excludes redeemed פסולי המוקדשין
steps.stepSummary: For רבי מאיר, the פסוק teaches that after פסולי המוקדשין are redeemed, you may make a מום on them, even though shearing and work are still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it excludes disqualified consecrated animals after they were redeemed. You might have thought that since shearing and work on them are still forbidden, making a מום is also forbidden. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer for רבי מאיר: 'תמים' excludes פסולי המוקדשין after their פדיון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeemed פסולי המוקדשין still keep some איסורים, since you may not shear them or work with them. So one could have thought making a מום on them is also forbidden. The פסוק teaches that this איסור does not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated animals that became unfit for a קרבן (usually through a מום)
Their redemption (exchanging their קדושה onto money)
You might have thought to say
It teaches us (that it is not so)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that redeemed פסולי המוקדשין are a middle category. Some איסורים stay on them and others fall away.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to exclude disqualified consecrated animals
after their redemption.
It might enter your mind to say:
since they are forbidden in shearing and labor,
let them also be forbidden regarding a blemish,
phrases.notes: Both words mean 'let them be forbidden'. The round-bracket form is in the standard print, and the square-bracket form is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְמַעוֹטֵי פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁים לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 7 with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the פסוק to a different, non-obvious case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since shearing and work stay forbidden after פדיון, making a מום should stay forbidden too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Making a מום on redeemed פסולי המוקדשין is permitted.

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with 'כל מום'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now challenges the רבנן: the פסוק 'כל מום לא יהיה בו' seems to forbid every מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the רבנן too, isn't it written 'There shall not be any blemish in it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the רבנן and asks how they handle רבי מאיר's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כל מום' sounds like it widens the איסור to every case, even an animal that is already blemished. The רבנן permit that case, so they must explain what 'כל מום' teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: There shall not be any blemish in it

phrases.english: And according to the Rabbis as well,
isn't it written: "There shall not be any blemish in it"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:21. This is רבי מאיר's source from step 5.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 6, now challenging the other side.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's view that making a מום on a blemished animal is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'כל מום' seems to include every blemish, even on an animal that is already blemished.

steps.title: The רבנן need that פסוק for a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that they use 'כל מום' for a different teaching, which is found in a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need that פסוק for what was taught in a ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן say the פסוק is already being used for something else. This line sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק that is busy teaching one law cannot also be used for the case of a blemished animal. The next step shows what that other law is.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
For that which was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: That verse is needed for that which was taught:

steps.terutzResolutionType: The פסוק is needed for a separate teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'כל מום' extends the איסור to an already blemished animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כל מום' is used for a different law, given in the ברייתא.

steps.title: You may not cause a מום even indirectly
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the extra word 'כל' that you may not even arrange for something else to cause the מום, like putting dough on the ear so a dog bites it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Any blemish shall not be in it.' From 'מום' alone I would only know not to make a blemish yourself. How do we know you may not cause one through others, such as putting dough or pressed figs on its ear so a dog will come and take it? The פסוק says 'כל מום'. It could have said just 'מום', and it said 'כל מום'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא teaches that the extra word 'כל' forbids causing a מום indirectly, through something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מום' alone forbids making the blemish directly. The extra 'כל' adds the indirect case, where a dog does the damage because of what the person set up. So for the רבנן, 'כל' is used here and says nothing about an already blemished animal.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר uses 'תמים' for redeemed פסולי המוקדשין, and the רבנן use 'כל מום' for causing a מום indirectly. That is how each side keeps its own view.

phrases.english: "There shall not be any blemish in it" —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בּוֹ מוּם,
phrases.english: I have only that there may not be a blemish in it.
phrases.notes: He means from the word 'מום' alone, you'd only know not to make the blemish yourself.

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא יִגְרוֹם לוֹ עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים,
phrases.english: From where do we know one may not cause it through others,
that one may not place dough or pressed figs
on the ear
so that a dog will come and take it?
phrases.notes: The dog grabs the food and bites off part of the ear, leaving a מום.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "Any blemish."
It says "blemish" and it says "any blemish."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל מוּם לֹא יִהְיֶה בּוֹ – אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בּוֹ מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the content of the ברייתא that step 11 pointed to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to cause a מום on a קדשים animal even indirectly, through another agent.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For the רבנן, 'כל מום' teaches the איסור of indirect damage, not an איסור on an already blemished animal.

steps.title: Leaven placed on dough that rises by itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי rules that someone who puts שאור on the dough of a מנחה and walks away is חייב when it becomes חמץ by itself, just like on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי says: if a person put leaven on top of dough, then went and sat down, and the dough became leavened on its own, he is liable for it, just like an action on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי אמי. A person who starts the leavening and then does nothing more is still חייב for making the מנחה into חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person only did one small act: putting the שאור on the dough. Everything after that happened by itself. רבי אמי still counts him as the one who made it חמץ, and he compares this to how liability works for מלאכה on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Sourdough leaven, a very sour dough used to make other dough rise
It became חמץ (leavened) on its own
Doing a forbidden מלאכה on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the person is free just because the dough rose 'by itself.' רבי אמי's whole point is that starting the process is enough to make him חייב.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami says:
If one placed leaven on top of dough,
phrases.notes: He means the dough of a מנחה, which is not allowed to become חמץ.

phrases.english: and he went and sat himself down,
and it became leavened on its own,
he is liable for it, like an action on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to leavening a מנחה, the topic of Step 2 (מחמץ אחר מחמץ). It adds a new ruling about someone who only starts the leavening and lets it finish by itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Putting שאור on a מנחה dough that then becomes חמץ by itself makes the person חייב, the same as doing a מלאכה on שבת.

steps.title: Is one really liable on שבת in such a case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי אמי's comparison to שבת and starts to bring a statement of רבה בר בר חנה against it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on שבת, is a person really liable in a case like this? But didn't רבה בר בר חנה say...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison to שבת. It is setting up a source from רבה בר בר חנה, which is quoted on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי's ruling depends on the idea that on שבת you are חייב even when the result finishes by itself. The גמרא doubts that this is true. It is about to show that רבה בר בר חנה seems to say otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [he] say? Brings a source that seems to disagree

phrases.english: And an action on Shabbat in a case like this,
is one liable?
But didn't Rabba bar bar Ḥana say...

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֵׂה שַׁבָּת כִּי הַאי גַּוְונָא מִי מִיחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison to שבת that רבי אמי used in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's claim that on שבת one is חייב even when the result happens by itself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If on שבת a person is not חייב when he only starts something and it finishes by itself, then רבי אמי's comparison falls apart. The proof from רבה בר בר חנה is about to be quoted.
